notes.text: A flaw was found in Starlette, a lightweight ASGI (Asynchronous Server Gateway Interface) framework. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted HTTP `Host` request header. This malformed header could cause the `request.url` to be incorrectly reconstructed, leading to a discrepancy with the actual requested path. Consequently, security restrictions enforced by middleware and endpoints that rely on `request.url` for validation could be bypassed, potentially allowing unauthorized access or actions.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: starlette: Starlette: Security restriction bypass via malformed HTTP Host header
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
The impact of this vulnerability is rated Moderate. A malformed Host header can manipulate the reconstructed request.url.path, introducing a discrepancy with the canonical ASGI request path (scope["path"]). However, the vulnerability does not directly grant access, modify routing, or bypass security controls on its own. A path-based authentication or authorization bypass is possible only if an application depends on request.url.path for access control decisions rather than the canonical ASGI path or standard framework mechanisms. The impact relies heavily on downstream application design rather than a default library failure.

Red Hat Satellite / Insights (IoP): The starlette package is included as a dependency of Connexion, but this flaw is rated Low impact because these services do not use path-based authentication middleware and all services are deployed behind reverse proxies. 

OpenShift Lightspeed (OLS): The starlette package is included as a dependency, but this flaw is rated Low impact because authentication is enforced via Kubernetes TokenReview/SubjectAccessReview through FastAPI dependency injection, not path-based middleware; request.url.path is only used for metrics and response header application.

RHOAI Kubeflow Training images: starlette is being used as indirect dependency of mlflow, but this flaw is rated as Low impact because mlflow is used as client library only to store training metrics on remote server, it doesn't expose any endpoint.

RHOAI odh-automl: The impact is reduced to Low since starlette is only used in the backend and it's transient dependency and starlette is not used at all to serve any endpoints.

RHOAI odh-kserve-autogluon-server-rhel9: While the Starlette dependency is present in the build, the vulnerable code in starlette is not reachable. This reduces the impact to low.
notes.title: Statement

Deploying an RFC-compliant reverse proxy (such as nginx, Apache, HAProxy, or Caddy) in front of the ASGI server will reject malformed Host headers before they reach the application. This is the most straightforward mitigation that does not require code changes.

If custom middleware is present, it should be updated to use `request.scope["path"]` instead of `request.url.path` for any security decisions. The ASGI scope path is derived from the HTTP request line and is not influenced by the Host header, so it reflects the actual request target.

notes.text: A flaw was found in vLLM, an inference and serving engine for large language models (LLMs). This vulnerability, residing in ASGI web servers and Starlette's trust in them, allows an attacker to bypass the OpenAI API Authentication Middleware. This bypass enables unauthorized access to the API without requiring the configured VLLM_API_KEY or --api-key, leading to critical unauthorized operations.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: vllm: starlette: vLLM: Critical authentication bypass allows unauthorized API access
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: CVE-2026-48746 is an authentication bypass in the vLLM OpenAI-compatible API server. A remote attacker who can reach the vLLM endpoint directly can craft a Host header so the authentication middleware checks a different URL path than the one actually dispatched, bypassing VLLM_API_KEY / --api-key protection. Successful exploitation allows unauthorized inference API access, which can result in confidentiality loss (model/prompt abuse) and availability impact (resource exhaustion). The flaw does not provide integrity compromise or arbitrary code execution. Exploitation requires vLLM API-key authentication to be enabled and the service to be exposed without an RFC-conforming reverse proxy that normalizes the Host header. Because Red Hat AI inference offerings are commonly deployed behind OpenShift Routes or similar proxies, and because the vulnerability is conditional on deployment and configuration, the overall flaw impact is rated Important rather than Critical.

cwe.name: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition

notes.text: A flaw was found in ONNX. The `save_external_data` function is vulnerable to symlink following and path traversal. A local attacker with write access to a directory where a victim serializes external data can exploit this by pre-planting a symlink. This allows the attacker to cause the victim's write operation to append to arbitrary files, potentially leading to unauthorized modification of critical system files.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: onnx: ONNX: Arbitrary file write via symlink following and path traversal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An IMPORTANT severity flaw was found in ONNX, affecting Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI) components that ship a vulnerable onnx version. The save_external_data function builds the external-data file path from the model's external_data location field and opens it for writing without symlink protections (O_NOFOLLOW/O_EXCL), after a non-atomic os.path.isfile() check. A local attacker with write access to a directory in which a victim serializes ONNX external data can exploit this time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition by pre-planting a symlink that is followed when the victim saves the model, causing the victim's write to append to arbitrary files the victim can write, such as ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, cron files, or application configuration files. Successful exploitation can result in unauthorized modification of critical files and further compromise of the victim's account. Exploitation requires local access, write access to the serialization directory, and that the victim save a model with external data; the attack vector is therefore local, not remote. Within RHOAI, the components that ship a vulnerable onnx version are affected, and a fix is being pursued through the responsible delegated product team; the remaining evaluated RHOAI components are not affected because they ship an onnx version that already contains the fix. Red Hat has rated this flaw as having a security impact of IMPORTANT.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in React Router. An unauthenticated attacker can send targeted requests to the manifest endpoint, leading to a denial of service (DoS). This can put a heavy load on the server, significantly slowing down response times and impacting the availability of the application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: react-router: @remix-run/server-runtime: React Router: Denial of Service via unauthenticated manifest endpoint requests
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
React Router (npm packages react-router and @remix-run/server-runtime) versions 7.0.0 through 7.17.0 expose an unauthenticated manifest endpoint. Repeated, targeted requests to this endpoint place heavy load on the server and can degrade or deny service for other users. This issue is a follow-up to CVE-2026-42342 and is fixed upstream in react-router/@remix-run/server-runtime 7.18.0.

This flaw only affects React Router's Framework Mode, applications that run a Node.js SSR server via @remix-run/server-runtime and serve the manifest endpoint. Applications using Declarative Mode (<BrowserRouter>) or Data Mode (createBrowserRouter/<RouterProvider>) do not run this server-side code path and are not affected. Simply bundling react-router does not by itself make a product exploitable; each console/UI component must be independently assessed by its owning team for Framework Mode usage and manifest endpoint exposure.

Red Hat's CVSS score (6.5, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H) is lower than the CVE.org score because the affected React Router components in Red Hat products are used in internal console UIs that are deployed behind authenticated ingress, reducing the practical attack surface. This mirrors the same re-scoring applied to the predecessor flaw, CVE-2026-42342, for the same endpoint family.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in Feast. This vulnerability allows unauthenticated or unauthorized attackers to achieve remote code execution. By sending a specially crafted gRPC request to the registry server, attackers can exploit an unsafe deserialization process. This enables them to execute operating system commands as the Feast service account, leading to a complete compromise of the affected system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: feast: Feast: Remote Code Execution via Unsafe Deserialization in gRPC Registry Server
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
Red Hat OpenShift AI ships Feast versions affected by CVE-2026-56121. This flaw allows remote code execution only against the Feast registry gRPC server (feast serve_registry, port 6570) when that service is running and reachable.

Default OpenShift AI installations are not affected. Installing OpenShift AI deploys the Feast operator but does not create a FeatureStore instance or start a registry server. The default FeatureStore configuration runs the online feature server only (feast serve), which does not expose the vulnerable gRPC endpoint. Workbench and pipeline runtime images include Feast as a client library and do not start a registry server.

Red Hat validated this by attempting exploitation against Feast 0.62.0: remote code execution succeeded only when a registry server was explicitly started; the default online-only configuration and library-only images were not exploitable.

Customers who configure a FeatureStore with an explicit registry server (registry.local.server) should treat this as a critical issue and apply the fix (Feast ≥ 0.63.0) when available. Enabling authorization alone does not remediate affected versions because unsafe deserialization occurs before authorization checks.

Red Hat rates this Important for OpenShift AI overall, reflecting that the vulnerable component is present but the attack surface is not exposed under default configurations.

cwe.name: Heap-based Buffer Overflow

notes.text: A heap buffer overflow vulnerability was found in libaom, the reference AV1 codec implementation. A flaw in the AV1 encoder's Look-Ahead Processing (LAP) mode causes the first-pass stats ring buffer wrap-around guard to be bypassed when g_lag_in_frames is set to 1 or higher. This results in a 232-byte out-of-bounds write on every encoded frame after the second, corrupting adjacent heap objects. An attacker who can influence encoder configuration in a transcoding service or WebRTC session could exploit this to cause a denial of service (process crash) or potentially achieve code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: libaom: libaom: heap buffer overflow in AV1 encoder first-pass stats buffer via LAP mode
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important severity because a heap buffer overflow with attacker-influenced data can cause reliable denial of service and potentially lead to code execution, though the attacker has only indirect control over the written values (encoder-computed statistics). In Red Hat products, libaom ships bundled within Firefox and Thunderbird as a statically-linked dependency used for AV1 decoding and WebRTC encoding. The vulnerable code path requires the encoder to be configured with g_lag_in_frames >= 1 (Look-Ahead Processing mode). In Firefox's WebRTC implementation, the encoder configuration is controlled by the browser itself and not exposed to remote peers, which significantly limits the attack surface compared to standalone transcoding services. RHEL-AI 3.4 and Hummingbird 1 ship standalone libaom (aom) packages at versions within the affected range. Applications on those platforms that use the libaom encoder API with LAP mode and accept untrusted configuration input are vulnerable.
notes.title: Statement

notes.title: CVSS score applicability

notes.text: An arbitrary address write vulnerability was found in libaom, the reference AV1 codec implementation. A missing bounds check in the SVC (Scalable Video Coding) layer ID control function allows an attacker to inject an arbitrary pointer into the cyclic refresh map field via crafted image pixel values. The encoder then writes approximately 1,200 bytes at the attacker-controlled address. This is fully deterministic and does not require a separate information leak. notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Critical severity because it provides a fully deterministic arbitrary address write primitive that requires no information leak and is self-bootstrapping from attacker-controlled pixel values. The 1,200-byte write at an attacker-chosen address is sufficient for control flow hijacking. In Red Hat products, libaom ships bundled within Firefox and Thunderbird. notes.text: A flaw was found in Micrometer's StatsD and Logging meter registries. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to inject line terminators into metric data, such as names or tag values, due to insufficient sanitization of untrusted input. Exploitation can lead to the spoofing of arbitrary metrics, including critical system or business metrics, and the injection of false log entries, potentially impacting monitoring and auditing systems.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: io.micrometer/micrometer-registry-statsd: io.micrometer/micrometer-core: Micrometer: Line-protocol and log injection via unsanitized input allows metric and log spoofing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A moderate severity flaw was found in Micrometer's StatsD and Logging meter registries (io.micrometer:micrometer-registry-statsd and io.micrometer:micrometer-core), which are shipped in a number of Red Hat middleware, integration, and application-platform products. These libraries do not sanitize newline characters (\n, \r) by default. When an application instruments meters using user-controlled, unvalidated input for metric names, tag keys, or tag values, a remote attacker can inject line terminators to break out of the current metric or log line. With the Datadog or Etsy flavor of the StatsD registry, whose protocol is newline-delimited, this enables line-protocol injection and cross-metric spoofing; with LoggingMeterRegistry, which prints metric output line-by-line to log files, this enables metric spoofing via downstream log-metrics scrapers or parsers as well as general log spoofing. A successful attacker can spoof arbitrary metrics, including critical system or business metrics, and inject false log entries, impacting the integrity of monitoring and auditing systems; the confidentiality and availability of the application itself are not directly affected. Exploitation requires the specific registry configuration together with unsafe instrumentation that passes untrusted input to meters, so attack complexity is high, and Red Hat rates this flaw Moderate (CVSS 3.1: 5.9, AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N), consistent with the upstream MEDIUM rating.

Multiple Red Hat products that ship the affected components, including Red Hat build of Quarkus, JBoss EAP XP, Red Hat Build of Keycloak, JBoss Data Grid, Red Hat AMQ, Red Hat OpenShift AI, and Red Hat build of Apache Camel, are recorded as affected, and fixes are being pursued by the responsible engineering teams; several affected product streams are out of active support scope. Red Hat Satellite is not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in the shipped candlepin component.

Exploitation requires that an application passes untrusted BER, CER, or DER input directly to the pyasn1 decoder — pyasn1 is a library and does not independently accept network input. Many common uses of pyasn1 involve parsing trusted certificates or local configuration and are not exposed to this flaw. The realistic impact is a denial-of-service of the consuming Python process, with automatic recovery in typical service deployments.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Netty (io.netty:netty-handler). When using the SslProvider.OPENSSL client path with a plain X509TrustManager and without Unsafe-based trust-manager wrapping (Java 25+), TLS hostname verification is disabled. This misconfiguration allows a man-in-the-middle attacker to present a fraudulent certificate for a different hostname, which is then accepted without proper validation. This could lead to sensitive information disclosure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: io.netty/netty-handler: Netty: TLS hostname verification bypass via OpenSSL client path misconfiguration
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat products ship io.netty:netty-handler as a transitive dependency across multiple middleware and platform products. While the CVSS score reflects the severity of a successful exploit — full confidentiality compromise of TLS-protected traffic without authentication — the vulnerable code path requires three conditions simultaneously: explicit OpenSSL provider configuration, a plain X509TrustManager, and a Java 25+ runtime. Most Red Hat product deployments use the default JDK SSL provider and currently run on Java 21 LTS, making the vulnerable configuration uncommon in practice.

This vulnerability only affects applications that explicitly configure Netty to use the OpenSSL TLS provider (SslProvider.OPENSSL). 

The following mitigations can reduce exposure without applying a patch:

1) Use the default JDK SSL provider — Do not configure SslProvider.OPENSSL in your Netty SslContext setup. The default JDK SSL provider (SslProvider.JDK) is not affected by this vulnerability. Most applications use the JDK default unless explicitly overridden.

2) Use X509ExtendedTrustManager — If the OpenSSL provider is required, ensure the configured trust manager extends X509ExtendedTrustManager rather than the plain X509TrustManager interface. The extended variant performs hostname verification independently of the Netty wrapping logic.

3) Run on Java 24 or earlier — The vulnerable code path only triggers on Java 25+ where sun.misc.Unsafe-based trust-manager wrapping is unavailable. Running on earlier Java versions (e.g., Java 21 LTS) means the wrapping works correctly and hostname verification stays enabled.

notes.text: A flaw was found in DOMPurify. When the `setConfig()` function is used with an `uponSanitizeAttribute` hook, the `ALLOWED_ATTR` allowlist is not properly cloned. notes.text: A flaw was found in nanoid (Nano ID), a small, secure, and URL-friendly unique string ID generator. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a zero-size input to the customAlphabet or customRandom functions. This would cause an infinite loop, leading to a denial of service (DoS) condition by hanging the application's calling thread.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: nanoid: nanoid: Denial of Service via infinite loop in random ID generation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An algorithmic denial of service flaw was found in the `nanoid` library. When calling `customAlphabet` or `customRandom` with a `size` parameter of `0`, the internal generation loop fails to meet its termination condition. In Node.js or browser execution contexts, an attacker who supplies an unvalidated, zero-value size parameter to these functions causes the thread to enter an infinite loop, driving CPU utilization to 100% and completely blocking event loop execution for that thread.

notes.text: A flaw was found in axios, a popular JavaScript library. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by providing malicious form data containing deeply nested field names. This input triggers uncontrolled recursion within the formDataToJSON function, which is responsible for processing form data. The excessive recursion exhausts the application's JavaScript call stack, leading to a denial of service for the affected request or, in some cases, causing the entire application process to terminate.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: axios: axios: Denial of Service via uncontrolled recursion in form data processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important flaw in the axios JavaScript library allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service. By submitting crafted form data with excessively nested bracket-delimited field names, an attacker can trigger uncontrolled recursion in the formDataToJSON function (exposed as axios.formToJSON() and used internally by the default transformRequest when FormData is sent with Content-Type: application/json), exhausting the JavaScript call stack and causing a RangeError that may terminate the application process. This vulnerability affects applications that pass attacker-controlled FormData field names to axios' FormData-to-JSON conversion.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in GitPython. A remote attacker can exploit a vulnerability in the Repo.clone_from() method by providing a specially crafted Git repository URL. This URL can contain references to environment variables, which are then expanded and included in the URL. This allows the attacker to exfiltrate sensitive environment variables, such as access keys or tokens, to an attacker-controlled server during the cloning process, leading to information disclosure.

notes.text: This Important vulnerability in GitPython allows for sensitive environment variable exfiltration. When an application utilizes GitPython's Repo.clone_from() method with an attacker-controlled Git repository URL, embedded environment variable tokens within the URL are expanded and transmitted to a remote server. This poses a risk of information disclosure, particularly for credentials or tokens, in Red Hat products that process untrusted clone URLs.

Exploitation requires the application to clone an attacker-controlled repository and then perform worktree operations against it; applications that only process trusted repositories are not exposed. notes.text: A flaw was found in fast-uri, a URI parser for Node.js. Its custom parser for bracketed IPv6 literals does not fully validate the IPv6 grammar, allowing invalid trailing text in an authority to be silently discarded. This issue affects Red Hat products that bundle fast-uri as part of their Node.js dependencies. Fixed versions are available: fast-uri 2.4.5, 3.1.6, and 4.1.3.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fast-uri, a software component used for parsing Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs) in Node.js applications. This vulnerability arises from an issue in how fast-uri processes the scheme part of a URI, specifically when it contains special characters that are percent-encoded. An attacker can exploit this by crafting a malicious URI, causing the parser to misinterpret the host, which can lead to serious security risks. These risks include unauthorized redirection to external websites, server-side request forgery (SSRF) where the application makes unintended requests to internal or external resources, and bypassing security policies.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fast-uri: fast-uri: URI parsing flaw enables server-side request forgery and redirects
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A host confusion vulnerability was found in fast-uri, a URI parser for Node.js. The parser runs a legacy decoding pass over the scheme component and never re-escapes the result. As a consequence, an input whose scheme carries percent-encoded slashes parses as having no authority (undefined host), yet resolving or normalizing that same input emits a network-path reference with an attacker-chosen authority. Applications that normalize or resolve untrusted URLs before a redirect check, host allowlist, or outbound request decision can be steered to an attacker-controlled domain, enabling server-side request forgery (SSRF), open redirect, or address-policy bypass. Additionally, a normalized URI in a response header can carry injected carriage return line feed (CRLF) characters, enabling HTTP response splitting attacks such as cache poisoning or session hijacking. This issue affects Red Hat products that bundle fast-uri as part of their Node.js dependencies. Fixed versions are available: fast-uri 2.4.5, 3.1.6, and 4.1.3.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: GitPython before 3.1.59 fails to safely re-serialize multi-line git-config values during write operations, corrupting dormant quoted values into injected directives like core.hooksPath. Attackers can craft config files with embedded newlines that become live git directives after any unrelated GitPython config write, enabling arbitrary code execution via hook invocation.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: gitpython: GitPython before 3.1.59 Remote Code Execution via Config Injection
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
Case for AC:H (8.1): the trigger needs two things the attacker does not
  straightforwardly own:
    (1) a crafted multi-line quoted value must already sit DORMANT in .git/config
        — the guarded set_value() path will not put it there; it must arrive via
        _read() of a file the attacker influenced but does not directly write; and
    (2) a SUBSEQUENT, UNRELATED GitPython config WRITE must fire to re-serialize
        and corrupt it — and that write is performed by the victim application on
        its own schedule, not by the attacker. 
    "Prepare the target environment" + "conditions beyond the attacker's control"
    is the textbook AC:H definition; step (2) in particular fits it.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GitPython. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to create arbitrary Git directories outside the intended clone destination. By manipulating the `separate_git_dir` parameter during repository cloning, an attacker can redirect repository metadata to an attacker-controlled filesystem path. This could lead to arbitrary directory creation and potentially enable the execution of malicious code through Git hooks.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: GitPython: GitPython: Arbitrary Code Execution via Path Traversal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat Product Security has identified a path traversal vulnerability in GitPython versions before 3.1.59. The vulnerability arises because the `--separate-git-dir` option is not included in the `unsafe_git_clone_options` denylist, allowing attackers who control the `separate_git_dir` parameter during repository cloning to redirect Git repository metadata to arbitrary filesystem locations outside the intended clone destination. This can lead to arbitrary directory and file creation bounded only by process permissions. When combined with subsequent Git operations that trigger hook execution on the redirected repository, this vulnerability can escalate to arbitrary code execution. Exploitation requires that the application passes untrusted, attacker-controlled input to the `separate_git_dir` keyword argument of `Repo.clone_from()` or `Repo.clone()` methods without proper validation, while the `allow_unsafe_options` parameter remains at its default value of False.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Tornado. An unauthenticated remote attacker could send a specially crafted request with a large number of fields in the URL-encoded body. This could cause the single-threaded event loop to stall, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) for all connections. The vulnerability occurs because the urllib.parse.parse_qs function is used without limiting the maximum number of fields.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: python-tornado: Tornado: Denial of Service via excessive URL-encoded body fields
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in Tornado's request body parsing mechanism. When processing application/x-www-form-urlencoded HTTP request bodies, Tornado invokes urllib.parse.parse_qs without specifying max_num_fields. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send an HTTP request with an excessively large number of form field key-value pairs. Parsing these fields synchronously blocks Tornado's single-threaded event loop, leading to a complete denial of service for all concurrent connections and incoming requests.

notes.text: qs: qs: Denial of Service via improper validation in stringify function
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A denial of service vulnerability was found in the qs package for Node.js. The stringify function does not verify that constructor.isBuffer is callable before invoking it. An attacker who can influence object shape, for example through query parameters parsed with allowPrototypes: true as Express 4 does by default, can cause qs.stringify to throw a TypeError when that data is re-serialized. In typical Node.js HTTP frameworks the error is caught per request and returns HTTP 500. In code paths without an error boundary, such as async handlers or background jobs, the process may exit.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An IMPORTANT severity flaw was found in ModelScope, a Python library included as a dependency in the KServe components of Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI). ModelScope parses model configuration files using PyYAML's unsafe yaml.Loader, which permits Python object construction tags in the YAML input to instantiate arbitrary objects. A remote attacker can craft a malicious model repository containing poisoned configuration files; when a user loads such a configuration, the attacker-supplied code executes in the context of the user's process, resulting in arbitrary code execution with high impact to confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Red Hat rates this flaw as IMPORTANT with a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.8 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), consistent with the upstream assessment; exploitation requires a user to load an attacker-supplied configuration file. The affected Red Hat OpenShift AI components are delegated to the RHOAI engineering team, whose analysis determined that the vulnerable code is not in the execute path of the shipped components, so it is not reachable through supported Red Hat OpenShift AI usage.

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici's BalancedPool component. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to bypass Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificate validation. The BalancedPool constructor incorrectly processes its options, silently discarding custom certificate validation functions. Consequently, a peer with an otherwise untrusted certificate may be accepted, potentially compromising the integrity of secure communication.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: TLS certificate validation bypass in BalancedPool via dropped connect options
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This flaw only affects applications that construct an undici BalancedPool with a function-valued connect or tls option — for example, a custom checkServerIdentity callback or connector used for certificate pinning across multiple upstreams. Client, Pool, Agent, and RoundRobinPool destructure these options before the internal JSON-based clone and are not affected. An attacker able to present, on the network path, a TLS endpoint whose certificate the application's custom validator was written to reject — but which still satisfies Node.js's default hostname and chain checks — can have that certificate silently accepted when the connection goes through BalancedPool, enabling a man-in-the-middle attack against affected connections.
This affects undici versions from 7.24.1 up to 7.29.1 and from 8.0.0 up to 8.10.2.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. When the cache or deduplicate interceptor is directly composed onto a Client or Pool, the destination origin is omitted from cache and request-deduplication keys. This allows a remote attacker to perform cross-origin cache poisoning, leading to information disclosure and potentially a full authentication bypass. An attacker could exploit this by having a trusted origin accept a malicious token, without contacting the legitimate trusted origin.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: Authentication bypass via cross-origin cache poisoning due to missing origin isolation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This flaw is present in the undici HTTP client library used by Node.js. When an application composes undici's Cache or Deduplicate interceptor directly onto a Client or Pool object (rather than onto an Agent), the library's internal cache and in-flight-request deduplication keys omit the destination origin. As a result, a cached or in-flight response captured for one upstream origin can be returned for a request intended for a different, trusted origin whenever the method, path, and relevant headers match. In the most severe demonstrated scenario, this allowed an attacker-controlled JWT to be accepted by the application as though it had been validated against a legitimate, trusted issuer, without that issuer ever being contacted — resulting in a full authentication bypass.
Exploitation requires that the affected application attach the Cache or Deduplicate interceptor directly to a Client/Pool — the default Agent-based dispatch path is not affected, since Agent already carries the origin in its dispatch options — and that an attacker can influence or collide with the cache/deduplication key for at least one origin the application communicates with.).
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate impact because exploiting it requires an unhandled HTTP 500 error condition and direct access to the server's logging output. In Red Hat OpenShift AI, notebook workloads execute within managed container environments where log inspection is restricted to authorized cluster administrators and workload owners through platform access controls. Consequently, while authentication tokens present in request headers can be recorded without proper sanitization during server faults, unauthorized third parties cannot capture these credentials remotely without preexisting elevated privileges.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GitPython. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code. By failing to properly validate the git directory location, GitPython allows attackers to impersonate the git directory using tracked files such as gitdir, commondir, and HEAD. An attacker can then place a malicious pre-commit hook in the tracked hooks directory, which executes when a victim calls index.commit() on a cloned or opened repository.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GitPython. A remote attacker could exploit a regular expression denial of service (ReDoS) vulnerability by crafting a malicious commit object. Specifically, a malformed author field containing an unterminated angle bracket can cause excessive processing, leading to the exhaustion of CPU resources and a denial of service for over two minutes per commit access.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A regular expression denial of service vulnerability was found in GitPython when processing commit author and committer fields. The Actor.name_email_regex pattern exhibits quadratic backtracking when encountering malformed author fields containing unterminated angle brackets. An attacker who can introduce a crafted commit object into a repository that is subsequently processed by a GitPython application can cause excessive CPU resource consumption, leading to denial of service for over two minutes per commit access. This requires the application to parse commits from untrusted sources such as public git servers, tarballs, or automated import tools.

notes.text: A flaw was found in zstd-jni. This use-after-free vulnerability occurs because streams and contexts only hold a dictionary's shared lock during the load call, allowing the dictionary to be closed while still being referenced. A remote attacker could exploit this by closing a dictionary after associating it with a stream or context. Subsequent read or write operations would then access freed native memory, leading to silent data corruption or a Java Virtual Machine (JVM) crash, resulting in a denial of service.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the GridFS component of the MongoDB Python Driver (pymongo). The driver can treat a caller-supplied structured file identifier as a MongoDB query condition instead of a literal identifier. An authenticated user who can influence the identifier passed to GridFS download, delete, or rename operations may retrieve stored file content beyond the intended target, delete all GridFS chunks in the affected bucket (rendering stored files unreadable), or rename a file other than the intended target.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pymongo: MongoDB Python Driver: Data disclosure and denial of service via query-operator injection
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This vulnerability is rated as Important because an authenticated user who can influence a GridFS file identifier can delete all file chunks in the affected bucket, making stored files unreadable, and can retrieve or rename a file other than the intended target. Exploitation requires an application to pass a structured identifier, for example a dictionary containing MongoDB query operators, into GridFS download, delete, or rename APIs rather than a literal identifier such as an ObjectId or string.

pymongo is a client library. A deployment is exploitable only if it calls those GridFS APIs with attacker-influenced identifiers. Scalar identifiers are not interpreted as query conditions. Successful exploitation is limited to GridFS-stored file content. It does not by itself provide code execution or host compromise.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

There is no complete mitigation for applications that must accept untrusted structured GridFS file identifiers. The following measures reduce risk until a patched pymongo is available:

1. Pass only literal identifiers to GridFS download, delete, and rename operations (ObjectId, string, or integer). Do not pass dictionaries, BSON documents, or other structured values derived from user input.
2. Restrict which authenticated users can invoke GridFS operations, and do not expose GridFS APIs to untrusted clients.
3. If GridFS is not required, avoid using the gridfs module.

notes.text:
A flaw was found in go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver for version < 1.17.10 and < 2.9.1. 
Improper handling of data query elements in the GridFS component can lead to a file identifier being misinterpreted as a query. An authenticated user can exploit this to delete all GridFS file chunks, making stored file content unreadable, resulting in a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2: MongoDB Go Driver: Data deletion via query-operator injection in GridFS file IDs
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the MongoDB Go Driver. The GridFS component does not properly sanitize caller-supplied file identifiers before using them in database queries. A structured document passed as a file ID (for example, a BSON document containing query operators) is interpreted as a query condition rather than a literal match value. An authenticated attacker who can influence the file identifier passed to GridFS operations such as Delete, DownloadToStream, or OpenDownloadStream in an affected application can exploit this to delete all chunks in a GridFS bucket, resulting in permanent data loss and denial of service.
The practical impact depends on whether the product's code passes externally-controlled values as GridFS file identifiers.
notes.title: Statement

If upgrading go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver to version 1.17.10 (v1) or 2.9.1 (v2) is not immediately possible, the following steps can reduce exposure:
- Validate file identifiers before passing them to GridFS operations. Ensure that file IDs supplied by users or external systems are scalar values (e.g., primitive.ObjectID or string) and reject any structured BSON documents or maps. This prevents query operator injection.
- Restrict who can supply GridFS file identifiers. Do not allow unauthenticated or low-privilege users to directly control the file ID parameter in GridFS API calls (Delete, OpenDownloadStream, DownloadToStream, etc.).

This issue leads to information disclosure, allowing unauthorized access to cached responses containing other tenants' sensitive data, and may cause connected automated agents to execute unauthorized actions under victim credentials.

While exploitation requires valid API access to affected proxy routes, the shared caching mechanism compromises confidentiality and integrity across AI workloads. Deployments serving single-tenant workloads or environments where semantic caching is not shared between untrusted tenants face substantially reduced exposure.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw of IMPORTANT severity was found in the vLLM MoRIIO KV-transfer connector acknowledgement handling. The functions MoRIIOConnectorScheduler.request_finished, MoRIIOConnectorWorker.get_finished, and MoRIIOWrapper._handle_release_message in vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py allocate resources in response to the request_id and kv_transfer_params arguments without adequate limits. There is no impact on confidentiality or integrity. Red Hat rates this flaw as IMPORTANT (CVSS 3.1: 7.5, AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H) because of the high availability impact, whereas the upstream CVE record rates it MODERATE (CVSS 3.1: 5.3) with low availability impact. notes.text: A flaw was found in devalue, a JavaScript library for serializing values. The `stringify` and `uneval` functions incorrectly serialize Node Buffers by emitting the entire backing `ArrayBuffer` instead of only the view. This vulnerability allows for the disclosure of up to 64 KB of unrelated process memory, potentially including sensitive data from other in-flight requests, without authentication. This can occur in server-side-rendered frameworks when a public page processes a small Buffer.

Exploitation depends on the application serializing Node buffer instances on publicly accessible endpoints, limiting vulnerability exposure strictly to services that handle such data flows.

notes.text: A flaw was found in LightGBM. The software does not properly validate data within text models, which can be exploited by an attacker. By crafting a malicious model file, an attacker can trigger an out-of-bounds write during the SHAP prediction process. This vulnerability could lead to arbitrary code execution or a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: LightGBM: LightGBM: Out-of-bounds write via crafted model file
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An out-of-bounds write flaw rated IMPORTANT was found in LightGBM, which is shipped in Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI). LightGBM through 4.7.0 fails to validate child and split array values when parsing text model files. When a crafted model file containing invalid node references is loaded and used for SHAP (feature contribution) prediction, out-of-bounds writes occur at attacker-chosen offsets in the leaf_depth_ buffer, which could lead to arbitrary code execution or a denial of service. Exploitation requires a victim to load and process an attacker-supplied malicious model file; this required user interaction is reflected in the Red Hat CVSS 3.1 score of 7.8, which is lower than the upstream CVSS 4.0 score of 8.5. Within Red Hat OpenShift AI, components that bundle the vulnerable LightGBM library are affected and a fix is being pursued by the responsible business unit. Other RHOAI container images were reviewed and determined not affected because the LightGBM component is not present or the vulnerable code is not in the executed path.

notes.text: A flaw was found in LiteLLM. This vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker to achieve privilege escalation and account takeover by presenting a valid JSON Web Token (JWT) containing an unverified email address that matches an existing user account. Because the authentication process falls back to an email-based lookup without checking if the email is verified, the application associates the attacker's session with the victim's profile. As a result, an attacker can inherit administrative privileges, overwrite account identity bindings, and maintain persistent unauthorized access to administrative endpoints and API keys.

notes.text: litellm: LiteLLM: Privilege escalation via unverified email lookup in JWT authentication
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important severity rather than Moderate because a low-privileged authenticated user can achieve full privilege escalation and administrative takeover across the deployment. In Red Hat OpenShift AI and Ansible Automation Platform environments where LiteLLM integrates with external token issuers, the service omits confirmation of email claim validation during user mapping. An attacker with a valid token containing an unconfirmed target address can seize control of administrative accounts, gaining persistent access to management interfaces and exposed credential stores.

notes.text: A flaw was found in http-cache-semantics. Environments hosting multi-tenant web applications or reverse proxies that evaluate HTTP cache headers via this component face direct exposure to cross-session credential disclosure.

This vulnerability allows Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) when pasting notebook cells from the system clipboard, as the application fails to clear trusted metadata flags from imported cell data. notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: jupyterlab: JupyterLab: Cross-Site Scripting via malicious clipboard cell pasting
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An IMPORTANT severity cross-site scripting (XSS) flaw was found in JupyterLab, which Red Hat ships within Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI) and Migration Toolkit for Applications offerings. When the useSystemClipboardForCells setting is enabled and pasteCodeCellsWithoutOutput is disabled (the default), the system clipboard cell-paste path accepts attacker-controlled cell JSON without clearing metadata.trusted. A pasted code cell can therefore mark its HTML output as trusted, bypass output sanitization, and execute attacker-supplied script in the authenticated JupyterLab origin as soon as the cell is pasted, without the user executing it. Running in the victim's session, the script can call the Jupyter Server REST API as that user, reading and writing any file under the server root, starting a kernel and running code in it, and opening a terminal where terminals are enabled. A remote attacker needs no JupyterLab account and no access to the server; exploitation requires enticing a user to copy malicious content and paste it into JupyterLab. Markdown and raw cells are not affected because their output is always sanitized. Red Hat's CVSS 3.1 score of 8.1 (IMPORTANT) matches the upstream score and reflects JupyterLab 4.5.0 and 4.5.1, where the system clipboard path is always active; from 4.5.2 the useSystemClipboardForCells setting is off by default, which lowers the practical attack complexity for deployments that keep that default. JupyterLab releases prior to 4.5.0, such as those bundled in some Red Hat OpenShift AI images, are not affected because the vulnerable system clipboard paste path was introduced in 4.5.0. This issue is delegated to the responsible Red Hat product teams and a fix is being pursued.

notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: An Important severity flaw was found in virtualenv, a tool for creating isolated Python virtual environments that is bundled as a dependency in a number of Red Hat products, including Red Hat OpenShift AI, Red Hat Enterprise Linux container images, Red Hat Hardened Images, and other Red Hat-delivered components. The generated activate (bash and zsh) and activate.fish scripts place path values that were already escaped by shlex.quote inside an additional quoted context. The surplus quotes can terminate the data-only quoted run, leaving shell metacharacters within a crafted value to be parsed as shell commands: in the bash and zsh scripts a crafted virtual environment path is interpolated when a relocated environment's recorded directory is absent, and in the fish script crafted Tcl or Tk library paths are interpolated into __TCL_LIBRARY__ or __TK_LIBRARY__. When a user sources such an activation script, an attacker who controls the crafted path can execute arbitrary code with the privileges of that user. The flaw was rated Important (CVSS 3.1 score 7.8, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), consistent with the upstream severity; exploitation requires local control of the affected path values and user interaction to source the activation script. notes.text: An IMPORTANT severity command injection flaw was found in virtualenv, a tool for creating isolated Python virtual environments that is shipped as a bundled dependency in Red Hat offerings such as Red Hat OpenShift AI, Red Hat Enterprise Linux UBI container images, Red Hat Hardened Images components, and Fedora/EPEL community projects. Some Red Hat components that bundle virtualenv are not affected because the vulnerable code or the component itself is not present in the shipped versions. For the affected Red Hat and community offerings the impact is rated IMPORTANT, and because virtualenv reaches these products as a dependency, fixes are being pursued through the delegated product and community maintainers rather than a direct Red Hat security update. notes.text: virtualenv: virtualenv: Arbitrary code execution via configuration injection in prompt values
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in virtualenv, a tool for creating isolated Python virtual environments that is bundled in a number of Red Hat offerings, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Red Hat OpenShift AI, and other layered products and containers, as well as in Fedora and EPEL community builds. Red Hat rates this flaw as having Moderate impact. virtualenv writes prompt values verbatim into the line-oriented pyvenv.cfg file, while its reader parses the file with str.splitlines() and accepts the last value for duplicate keys. An attacker who can influence prompt input -- the --prompt command-line option, the VIRTUALENV_PROMPT environment variable, or a configuration-derived value such as a CI job templating an untrusted branch name -- can inject line boundaries and additional configuration keys, including home, into the generated pyvenv.cfg. Because tooling reads home to locate the base interpreter, a consumer that trusts the file can be redirected to an attacker-selected interpreter, potentially resulting in arbitrary code execution or environment tampering when the virtual environment is used. Exploitation requires the prompt value to come from outside the operator's trust boundary: where the operator supplies the prompt directly, they already control the command line, and the effect is corruption of their own environment rather than privilege gain. This is why Red Hat assesses the impact as Moderate, while the upstream project published the advisory with low severity. Fixes for affected Red Hat products and streams are being pursued by the responsible component and product teams under delegated resolution; some community and out-of-support-scope streams will not receive an update.
notes.title: Statement

Strip line boundaries (such as newline, carriage return, and other Unicode line-separator characters) from any value before using it as --prompt or VIRTUALENV_PROMPT, and do not pass externally influenced data -- for example user-supplied strings or CI-derived values such as branch names -- as the virtualenv prompt. Ensure the VIRTUALENV_PROMPT environment variable and any configuration file that sets the prompt are sourced only from trusted input. The upstream project fixed this issue in virtualenv 21.7.11 by collapsing line boundaries when writing pyvenv.cfg, so updating to a version that contains this fix resolves the issue. For Red Hat products that bundle virtualenv, apply updates through the respective product channels.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Tornado. A remote malicious server can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) when an application using the CurlAsyncHTTPClient component fetches an untrusted web address. Because the client fails to enforce limits on incoming response sizes, the attacker can return a small, highly compressed payload (a decompression bomb) that expands to an enormous size. This unbounded memory consumption exhausts system resources and crashes the application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: tornado: Tornado: Denial of Service via decompression bomb in CurlAsyncHTTPClient
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability has been rated as Important because an untrusted remote server can remotely terminate an application process through memory exhaustion without requiring credentials. By default, Tornado deploys the SimpleAsyncHTTPClient implementation, which includes built-in thresholds for decompressed and raw payload sizes and remains unaffected by this flaw. However, systems that explicitly configure CurlAsyncHTTPClient—typically enabled for custom proxy routing or advanced transport options—bypass these protections and do not enforce body size constraints. When such client applications fetch resources from compromised or malicious web endpoints, the resulting decompression bomb can consume all available system memory, leading to an immediate denial of service.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For Red Hat OpenShift AI 3.4.5 see the following documentation, which will be updated shortly for this release, for important instructions on how to upgrade your cluster and fully apply this errata update:

https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai/

Restrict outbound HTTP client requests to trusted destinations and avoid using the CurlAsyncHTTPClient backend when fetching untrusted web content.

1. Application configuration: Configure Tornado applications to utilize the default SimpleAsyncHTTPClient instead of CurlAsyncHTTPClient, provided specialized libcurl functionality (such as custom proxy configurations or specific TLS options) is not required. The default client enforces strict size boundaries on compressed and uncompressed response bodies.
2. Network egress filtering: Implement firewall rules or egress network policies to restrict outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections exclusively to verified, trustworthy endpoints, preventing the client from contacting potentially malicious third-party servers.
3. Operational controls: Ensure that user-supplied or untrusted URLs are validated, sanitized, or rejected before initiating outbound retrieval requests.

Caveats: Switching the HTTP client backend from CurlAsyncHTTPClient to SimpleAsyncHTTPClient may disrupt services that depend on libcurl-specific features. Enforcing egress filtering may block connections to unlisted external services.

notes.text: A flaw was found in uv. An attacker could achieve arbitrary code execution on a Windows system by tricking a user into installing a specially crafted Python wheel package. During archive extraction, files can be written outside the intended target directory, allowing an attacker to place malicious executable files into locations within the system search path (PATH).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: uv: uv: Arbitrary code execution via malicious package extraction on Windows
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this IMPORTANT vulnerability in uv, a Python package and project manager written in Rust, which is shipped in affected Red Hat offerings across AI and development-tools components. During installation of a Python wheel on Windows, uv could be induced by a maliciously crafted wheel to write files outside the intended installation directory, including placing an executable into a directory already present on the user's PATH. By tricking a user into installing such a wheel, an attacker could achieve arbitrary code execution in the context of that user when the planted executable is subsequently invoked, compromising the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the user's account. Non-Windows hosts are not affected. The Red Hat severity of IMPORTANT (CVSS 3.1 score 7.8) differs from the upstream rating of MODERATE (CVSS 4.0 score 5.9) primarily because the upstream vector scores integrity-only impact requiring user interaction, while the Red Hat vector accounts for high impact to confidentiality, integrity, and availability within the user's security context.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fsspec. This vulnerability can lead to arbitrary code execution due to unrestricted template evaluation in the ReferenceFileSystem component. When processing filesystem reference metadata documents, template expressions are evaluated without security restrictions or sandboxing. A remote attacker can exploit this flaw by enticing a user or automated service to open a maliciously crafted reference file, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the running application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fsspec: fsspec: arbitrary code execution via unrestricted template rendering in ReferenceFileSystem
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an attacker could achieve arbitrary code execution within the application environment, though exploitation requires tricking a user or pipeline into opening an untrusted reference catalog. In typical Red Hat deployments such as Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI), fsspec is utilized for data manipulation and storage abstraction across containerized workloads. The impact is limited to the privileges of the running container or application process without granting immediate host-level access, which aligns the risk with an Important rather than a Critical rating.

notes.text: A flaw was found in probe-image-size. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying specially crafted Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) input. Due to inefficient pattern matching and input handling during SVG parsing, processing unclosed tags can consume excessive CPU resources and block the application event loop, leaving the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: probe-image-size: probe-image-size: Denial of Service via crafted SVG input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This issue is classified as Moderate severity because an unauthenticated remote attacker supplying specially crafted SVG input can trigger inefficient parsing, resulting in excessive CPU consumption and a denial of service (DoS) by blocking the application event loop without enabling arbitrary code execution or data exposure.

notes.text: A flaw was found in langgraph-sdk. This vulnerability allows an authenticated attacker to bypass authorization controls to access, modify, or delete resources belonging to other users. The issue occurs because resource-scoped authorization decorators fail to restrict handlers to specified actions, inadvertently registering wildcard handlers that override fallback permission and ownership checks.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: langgraph-sdk: langgraph-sdk: Authorization bypass via improper resource handler registration
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw is rated as having Important impact because authenticated remote users could bypass intended authorization boundaries in multi-tenant environments, resulting in unauthorized access or modification of sensitive resources. In Red Hat products integrating this SDK, exposure is limited to environments where custom authentication policies filter specific resource operations. Furthermore, the issue only presents a risk if the custom handler does not enforce permissions across all attempted operations independently.

notes.text: A flaw was found in docling. When configured to process LaTeX documents using the Tectonic engine, the application does not restrict TeX file operations during compilation. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting crafted document input to read sensitive files or overwrite existing files on the host system. In environments where shell escape features are enabled, this flaw may also permit arbitrary command execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: docling: docling: Arbitrary file read and write via unrestricted TeX primitives in Tectonic engine
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate severity vulnerability was found in docling, a document conversion library shipped in Red Hat OpenShift AI and Lightspeed Core offerings. When docling is explicitly configured to render LaTeX content with the Tectonic engine (LatexBackendOptions(tikz_engine="tectonic")), it compiles an untrusted TikZ body and document preamble without restricting TeX file primitives such as \openin and \openout. An attacker who can supply a crafted document for conversion can use these primitives to read files accessible to the converter process and to create or overwrite writable files on the host, impacting confidentiality, integrity, and availability. If the separate tikz_engine_allow_shell_escape option is also enabled, arbitrary command execution through TeX shell escapes is possible. The default docling configuration, which does not enable Tectonic rendering, is not affected. Red Hat rates this flaw moderate, lower than the upstream important rating, because exploitation requires a non-default configuration that explicitly enables the Tectonic engine and requires processing attacker-supplied input, resulting in a local attack vector with high attack complexity and required user interaction rather than the network vector assumed upstream. The affected Red Hat products are tracked as affected and fixes are being pursued through the responsible product teams.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

Avoid enabling the Tectonic TikZ engine when processing untrusted LaTeX documents. The default docling configuration does not enable Tectonic rendering and is not affected by this flaw, so deployments that have not opted into LatexBackendOptions(tikz_engine="tectonic") are not exposed. The tikz_engine_allow_shell_escape option, which additionally allows shell command execution through TeX, should not be enabled. For deployments that require Tectonic rendering of untrusted input, no mitigation other than upgrading to a release containing the upstream fix is currently available.

notes.text: A flaw was found in aws-smithy-json. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service (DoS) in smithy-rs generated servers. By sending a small HTTP request containing deeply nested JSON, the attacker can trigger uncontrolled recursion in the aws-smithy-json runtime, leading to stack exhaustion and a process abort. This can make the affected server unavailable to legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: aws-smithy-json: aws-smithy-json: Denial of Service via uncontrolled recursion with deeply nested JSON
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw in the `aws-smithy-json` runtime crate allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to trigger a denial of service by sending a crafted HTTP request with deeply nested JSON. Red Hat products utilizing `smithy-rs` generated servers, such as components in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and Red Hat Trusted Artifact Signer, are susceptible to service disruption if exposed to untrusted networks.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/html. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing specially crafted HTML. When this arbitrary HTML is parsed and rendered, it can result in an unexpected HTML tree, bypassing input sanitization. This can be leveraged to execute Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution in applications that use the affected component.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/html: golang.org/x/net/html: Arbitrary code execution via Cross-Site Scripting
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important vulnerability in `golang.org/x/net/html` could enable remote attackers to execute Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution. The flaw allows specially crafted HTML to bypass input sanitization during parsing and rendering. Red Hat products are affected if they process untrusted HTML content using the vulnerable component without additional output encoding or robust content security policies.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/html. When arbitrary HTML is parsed and then rendered, it can result in an unexpected HTML tree. This allows an attacker to bypass HTML sanitization mechanisms, leading to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks in applications. Such attacks can result in information disclosure or arbitrary code execution.

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/html: golang: golang.org/x/net/html: Cross-Site Scripting via HTML parsing bypass
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability in `golang.org/x/net/html` is rated as Important. It allows for Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks by enabling an attacker to bypass HTML sanitization mechanisms when arbitrary HTML is parsed and rendered. This can lead to information disclosure or arbitrary code execution in affected applications. Exploitation typically requires user interaction, where a user processes specially crafted malicious HTML content.

notes.text: A flaw was found in OpenTelemetry-Go, the Go implementation of OpenTelemetry. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending multiple 'baggage' header lines. The system's independent parsing and aggregation of each header field-value across multiple values can lead to amplified CPU and memory allocations, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go: OpenTelemetry-Go: Denial of Service via crafted multi-value baggage headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in OpenTelemetry-Go, affecting Red Hat Multicluster Engine for Kubernetes. A remote attacker can exploit this flaw by sending multiple crafted `baggage` HTTP header lines, leading to excessive CPU and memory consumption and potentially rendering services unavailable. This impact is significant due to the potential for widespread disruption in a multi-cluster environment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package within the Go (golang) standard library, specifically affecting TLS 1.3 connections. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending multiple key update messages in a single record after the handshake. This can cause the connection to deadlock, leading to uncontrolled consumption of resources and ultimately a denial of service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: Go crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple TLS 1.3 key update messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: A flaw in the Go `crypto/tls` package allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service in applications using TLS 1.3. By sending multiple key update messages in a single record post-handshake, an attacker can trigger a connection deadlock, leading to uncontrolled resource consumption. This impacts Red Hat products utilizing the affected Go standard library for TLS 1.3 connections.

notes.text: A flaw was found in github.com/buger/jsonparser. The Delete function, when processing malformed JSON input, fails to properly validate offsets. This vulnerability can lead to a negative slice index and a runtime panic, allowing a remote attacker to cause a denial of service (DoS) by providing specially crafted JSON data.

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go, the Go language implementation of gRPC. This vulnerability, an authorization bypass, is caused by improper input validation of the HTTP/2 `:path` pseudo-header. A remote attacker can exploit this by sending raw HTTP/2 frames with a malformed `:path` that omits the mandatory leading slash. This allows the attacker to bypass defined security policies, potentially leading to unauthorized access to services or information disclosure.

remediations.details: To mitigate this issue, implement infrastructure-level normalization to ensure all incoming HTTP/2 `:path` headers are properly formatted with a leading slash before reaching the gRPC-Go server. This can be achieved by configuring a reverse proxy or API gateway to validate and normalize the `:path` header. Ensure that any such intermediary is properly configured and restarted to apply the changes, which may temporarily impact service availability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/asn1` package in Go. An attacker could provide a specially crafted, deeply-nested Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) structure, leading to excessive recursion during the `Unmarshal` operation. This could result in stack exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go encoding/asn1 package, as it can be triggered remotely without authentication. An attacker can provide a malformed ASN.1 structure, causing excessive recursion during unmarshalling and leading to stack exhaustion, which can render the service unavailable.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the SPDY streaming code used by Kubelet, CRI-O, and kube-apiserver. An attacker with specific cluster roles, such as those allowing access to pod port forwarding, execution, or attachment, or node proxying, could exploit this vulnerability. This could lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) by causing the affected components to become unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: Kubelet: CRI-O: kube-apiserver: Kubelet, CRI-O, kube-apiserver: Denial of Service via SPDY streaming code
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw affecting OpenShift Container Platform. An attacker with specific elevated cluster roles, such as those permitting pod port forwarding, execution, attachment, or node proxying, could exploit a vulnerability in the SPDY streaming code of Kubelet, CRI-O, and kube-apiserver, leading to unresponsiveness of these critical components.

remediations.details: To mitigate this issue, review and restrict the assignment of Kubernetes cluster roles `pods/portforward (create)`, `pods/exec (create)`, `pods/attach (create)`, and `nodes/proxy (get/create)` to untrusted users or service accounts. Ensure that only authorized and necessary entities possess these permissions. Modifying RBAC policies can impact the functionality of applications and services that rely on these permissions; careful testing is recommended.

notes.text: A flaw was found in OpenTelemetry-Go. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending oversized or invalid baggage headers. The `Parse` function, in affected versions, failed to reject raw-length inputs, leading to excessive processing and error logging when handling these large inputs.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go: go.opentelemetry.io/otel/baggage: go.opentelemetry.io/otel/propagation: OpenTelemetry-Go: Denial of Service via oversized baggage headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in OpenTelemetry-Go, affecting versions 1.41.0 and 1.43.0. An attacker can exploit this flaw by sending oversized baggage headers, causing the `Parse` function to process invalid inputs and log errors, which can lead to resource exhaustion and service disruption in Red Hat products utilizing these affected OpenTelemetry-Go versions. The impact is considered Important due to the potential for remote, unauthenticated denial of service.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Prometheus, an open-source monitoring system. The `client_secret` field within the Azure Active Directory (AD) remote write OAuth configuration was incorrectly handled as a plain string instead of a secure Secret type. This misconfiguration allowed any user or process with access to the `/-/config` HTTP API endpoint to view the Azure OAuth client secret in plaintext. This vulnerability leads to information disclosure, potentially compromising the security of integrated Azure AD services.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/prometheus/prometheus: Prometheus: Information disclosure of Azure OAuth client secret via config API
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Important information disclosure flaw in Prometheus affects instances configured to use Azure AD remote write with OAuth authentication. The client secret, intended to be a secure credential, is exposed in plaintext through the `/-/config` HTTP API endpoint. This could allow an attacker with access to this endpoint to retrieve the secret, potentially compromising integrated Azure AD services.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Prometheus. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit the remote read endpoint (`/api/v1/read`) by sending a specially crafted, small snappy-compressed payload. This payload causes a disproportionately large memory allocation, leading to memory exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) by crashing the Prometheus process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/prometheus/prometheus: Prometheus: Denial of Service via uncontrolled memory allocation in remote read endpoint
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in Prometheus, allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to crash the Prometheus process. This could lead to service unavailability in Red Hat products that deploy Prometheus for monitoring, as the remote read endpoint does not properly validate snappy-compressed request lengths.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/mail` package within the Go standard library. A remote attacker could provide specially crafted, pathological email addresses. When these malformed email addresses are parsed by the `consumePhrase` function, it can lead to excessive resource consumption due to quadratic string concatenation, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/mail: golang: net/mail: Denial of Service via pathological email address parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `net/mail` package of the Go standard library. A remote attacker can exploit this flaw by sending specially crafted email addresses, leading to excessive resource consumption and a denial of service in Go applications that parse email addresses using the affected library.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/html. This vulnerability allows an attacker to manipulate how HTML is processed and displayed. By providing specially crafted HTML, an attacker can cause an unexpected structure in the rendered output. This can lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks, where malicious scripts are executed in a user's web browser, potentially compromising user data or taking control of their session.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/html: golang: golang.org/x/net/html: Cross-Site Scripting via unexpected HTML tree rendering
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw in golang.org/x/net/html can lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in applications that parse and render untrusted HTML, even with sanitization attempts. This is due to an unexpected HTML tree structure, allowing malicious scripts to execute in a user's browser.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/dns/dnsmessage. A remote attacker could send a specially crafted Service Binding (SVCB) or HTTPS resource record (RR) to a system using this component. When parsing this invalid record, the system may panic due to a parameter value overflowing the message buffer. This can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) condition, making the affected system unavailable.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/text. The norm.Iter component can enter an infinite loop when processing input that contains invalid UTF-8 (Unicode Transformation Format - 8-bit) bytes. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing specially crafted input, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) condition where the affected application becomes unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/text: golang.org/x/text: Denial of Service via invalid UTF-8 input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: This flaw in the `golang.org/x/text` library can lead to a denial of service. An attacker could provide specially crafted invalid UTF-8 input to an application using the affected `norm.Iter` functionality, causing it to enter an infinite loop and become unresponsive.
